provenance: Adapter metadata captured from the previously published manifest after verifying its full code/source digest. Capture is not model execution.

1.name: AlexNet
1.mechanism: Five convolution layers and three fully connected layers from torchvision; reduced classifier.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Torchvision uses its documented AlexNet variant; adaptive pooling 1x1 and classifier width 128 replace the 6x6/4096 head.

2.name: ResNet
2.mechanism: ResNet-18 BasicBlock residual stages, directly instantiated from torchvision.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Input is a synthetic 32-pixel grayscale image repeated to RGB; classifier has three classes.

3.name: DenseNet
3.mechanism: Dense concatenation and compressed transition layers in the upstream DenseNet class.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

4.name: ConvNeXt
4.mechanism: Depthwise 7x7 convolution, channels-last LayerNorm, inverted bottleneck and layer scale.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

5.name: FCN
5.mechanism: FCN-8s: VGG pool3/pool4 score fusion plus learned 2x/2x/8x transposed upsampling.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Reduced VGG channels/FC widths; same-padding replaces the original padding/cropping boundary convention.

6.name: U-Net
6.mechanism: Two convolutions per scale, contracting path, transposed upsampling and concatenated encoder skips.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Three pooling levels and same-padding instead of the original four-level valid-convolution/crop preset.

7.name: 3D U-Net
7.mechanism: Volumetric convolution/pooling/upsampling and same-scale 3D encoder skips with BatchNorm.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Reduced channels; same-padding; densely labelled phantoms do not reproduce the sparse-annotation study.

8.name: V-Net
8.mechanism: MONAI VNet residual volumetric stages with 5x5x5 kernels; soft Dice training objective.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
MONAI implementation with ELU, dropout disabled and two output classes; 32-cube teaching input.

10.name: UNETR
10.mechanism: Twelve-layer ViT encoder with intermediate token features decoded by a volumetric U-shaped network.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

11.name: Swin UNETR (architecture)
11.mechanism: Hierarchical shifted-window transformer encoder and volumetric skip decoder.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
This lesson runs the segmentation architecture. The original SSL rotation/contrast/restoration pretraining and its checkpoint are NOT reproduced.
GroupNorm replaces InstanceNorm to support tiny spatial grids.

12.name: MedNeXt
12.mechanism: Authors' MedNeXt encoder/decoder and depthwise inverted bottleneck blocks, with only a local import adapter.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Width 4, one block per scale, expansion 2 and kernel 3; original scaling/training/UpKern experiment is not reproduced.

13.name: Models Genesis (pretext mechanisms)
13.mechanism: Restore 3D inputs after local shuffling, Bezier intensity transformation, inpainting or outpainting.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Independent PyTorch teaching implementation; reduced 3D U-Net and corruption budget; no published pretrained model or transfer result.

15.name: S4
15.mechanism: Authors' full diagonal-plus-low-rank S4 kernel, HiPPO initialization and FFT convolution.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Single-process logging adapter; naive CPU Cauchy kernel instead of accelerated kernels; small classifier added.

16.name: Mamba
16.mechanism: Authors' Mamba block, input-dependent delta/B/C, causal depthwise convolution and exact reference selective scan.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Python reference scan is slower than CUDA fused kernels; small sequence classification head added.

17.name: VMamba (SS2D mechanism)
17.mechanism: Four independent selective scans along row/column orders and their reversals; restored 2D alignment and gated fusion.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Independent compact SS2D port with a small image stem/head; not the complete VSSM hierarchy, initialization or ImageNet recipe.

18.name: U-Mamba (bottleneck mechanism)
18.mechanism: Residual convolution U-shaped encoder/decoder with authors' Mamba block on flattened bottleneck features.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Compact bottleneck variant only; nnU-Net planning and the full U-Mamba_Bot/Enc training pipelines are not reproduced.

19.name: SegMamba (spatial scan mechanism)
19.mechanism: Gated spatial convolution branches and three sequence scan orders inside a volumetric skip network.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
The three-order scan is a pedagogical analogue, not the authors' BiMamba-v3/fast-slice kernel or complete SegMamba architecture.

20.name: Transformer
20.mechanism: Encoder-decoder multihead attention, sinusoidal positions, causal target mask and teacher-forced token loss.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Small vocabulary and token reversal exercise instead of machine translation; no WMT training recipe.

21.name: Vision Transformer / ViT
21.mechanism: Patch projection, class token, learned positional embeddings and pre-norm transformer encoder.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

22.name: Swin Transformer
22.mechanism: Alternating regular/shifted window attention, relative position bias and patch merging.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

23.name: Mask2Former (masked-attention mechanism)
23.mechanism: Query masks restrict cross-attention; bipartite matching supervises class/mask/dice set predictions.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Small convolution pixel decoder replaces multi-scale deformable attention; semantic foreground/background targets, not panoptic instance annotations.
Matching, mask attention and set losses are real; the full Detectron2 pipeline is not reproduced.

24.name: SimCLR
24.mechanism: Two independent views, nonlinear projection and symmetric NT-Xent; self-similarities excluded.
limitations: Small patch Transformer replaces the original ResNet; grayscale synthetic augmentations; no ImageNet-scale batch/training.

25.name: MoCo
25.mechanism: Gradient-trained query encoder, stopped EMA key encoder, and a FIFO negative queue.
limitations: Paper-equation CPU implementation; no copying of upstream code with unresolved license. Small encoder/queue, no distributed shuffle BN.

26.name: MAE
26.mechanism: Author encoder sees only visible patches; a lightweight decoder reconstructs masked pixels.
limitations: Author source, CC BY-NC-4.0. Shrunk image/patch/width/depth; no pretrained weights. RGB obtained by repeating the grayscale teaching image.

27.name: DINO
27.mechanism: Cross-view student–teacher distillation with stopped EMA teacher, centering and sharpened teacher probabilities.
limitations: Independent two-view mechanism implementation, not copied author DINO code. No multi-crop schedule, weight-normalized final layer or original training recipe.

28.name: iBOT
28.mechanism: Global distillation plus patch-token distillation from unmasked teacher to masked student.
limitations: Shared-head two-view mechanism exercise; simplified mask sampler/encoder and no original training schedule or weights.

29.name: DINOv2
29.mechanism: DINO-style global and masked patch distillation with a nearest-neighbor entropy regularizer.
limitations: Mechanism subset only: local mini objectives do not reproduce DINOv2 data curation, Sinkhorn teacher balancing, untied heads, large training or learned representations.

30.name: CLIP
30.mechanism: Original OpenAI ViT image encoder, causal text Transformer, EOT pooling, learned logit scale and symmetric image–text contrastive loss.
limitations: Unmodified MIT author architecture with smaller dimensions and random initialization; no pretrained weights or foundation-pretraining claim.

Synthetic grayscale images are repeated into RGB. A 32-token teaching vocabulary replaces byte-pair tokenization; EOS=2 is explicitly remapped to the largest token ID required by original CLIP pooling.
Paired diagonal contrastive targets are retained. Repeated short synthetic descriptions can be false negatives; tiny batches do not establish semantic retrieval or zero-shot quality.

31.name: BLIP-2 (stage-two bridge architecture)
31.mechanism: Pinned Transformers BLIP-2 ViT, learned query tokens, Q-Former cross-attention, projection and frozen OPT causal language model; train only the stage-two visual-language bridge.
limitations: Canonical Apache-2.0 library implementation, not copied Salesforce LAVIS training code. All modules start randomly initialized at reduced dimensions; frozen random ViT/OPT have no pretrained visual or language knowledge.

Only the stage-two bridge architecture and causal caption loss are exercised. Stage-one image-text contrastive, image-text matching and image-grounded generation pretraining, instruction tuning and real caption data are absent.

Synthetic vocabulary replaces the original tokenizer. Vision initialization and learned query tokens use normal std=0.02 to avoid the library checkpoint-oriented near-zero/zero defaults. No image-captioning or question-answering capability is claimed.

32.name: Segment Anything (SAM)
32.mechanism: Original window/global ViT, Fourier point/box prompt encoder, two-way attention decoder, three ambiguity masks, IoU head, and error-guided correction with previous-mask prompts.
limitations: Unmodified Apache-2.0 author architecture at reduced image size/width/depth with random initialization; no MAE initialization, SA-1B pretraining, or zero-shot performance claim.

Teaching training uses an initial supplied foreground point and two prompt rounds by default. The 11-round mixed point/box schedule, noisy boxes, large-scale data engine and original optimizer schedule are not reproduced.

Mask supervision uses minimum-over-candidate 20× focal + Dice; IoU regression supervises every returned candidate. Default supplied synthetic prompts come from ground truth and are explicit inputs, not predicted detections.

33.name: MedSAM
33.mechanism: Original MedSAM image/prompt/mask modules, box-only prompts, frozen prompt encoder, and author squared-prediction Dice plus BCE training objective.
limitations: Unmodified Apache-2.0 MedSAM architecture at reduced dimensions. Random initialization replaces SAM/MedSAM checkpoints; this is the fine-tuning mechanism on synthetic data, not a pretrained medical model.

The original MedSAM [0,1] input convention is retained. Synthetic grayscale is repeated into RGB; supplied tight boxes replace the original randomly perturbed training boxes and medical preprocessing.
The prompt encoder stays frozen as in the author training script. IoU scores are returned for inspection but are not trained by MedSAM's Dice+BCE objective. No clinical data or performance claim.

43.name: Deep Autoencoder
43.mechanism: Layerwise contrastive-divergence RBM pretraining, Gaussian bottleneck, then unfolded untied autoencoder fine-tuning.
limitations: Two compact RBMs replace the paper's large four-layer example; default first two training calls pretrain and later calls fine-tune.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

44.name: GAN
44.mechanism: Separate discriminator and non-saturating generator gradients implement the two-player game.
limitations: Small MLP generator/discriminator; one simultaneous update instead of a tuned adversarial training schedule.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

45.name: pix2pix
45.mechanism: Original recursive U-Net and 70x70 conditional PatchGAN with logistic adversarial and paired L1 objectives.
limitations: Width 8 and five U-Net downsamplings at 64px; default examples are synthetic noisy/clean pairs.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

46.name: CycleGAN
46.mechanism: Original ResNet generators and PatchGANs; dual LSGAN, cycle and identity losses on shuffled domains.
limitations: Three residual blocks; no replay buffer or long-horizon learning-rate schedule; synthetic domain translation only.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

47.name: FBPConvNet
47.mechanism: A discrete parallel-beam ramp-filtered backprojection precedes residual image-domain U-Net refinement.
limitations: Reduced U-Net and pixel-driven teaching projector; not the original MatConvNet/CT geometry implementation.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

48.name: Learned Primal-Dual
48.mechanism: Five-channel primal and dual memories update through distinct CNNs and explicit A and its exact transpose at every stage.
limitations: Three stages and a 16px parallel-beam phantom replace the full ODL experiment.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

49.name: Variational Network
49.mechanism: MRI energy-gradient updates use constrained convolution filters, learned RBF influence functions and coil-aware Fourier data gradients.
limitations: Small filter bank and three stages; synthetic smooth coil maps are supplied, not learned.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

50.name: MoDL
50.mechanism: One shared residual CNN alternates with differentiable CG solves of (A* A + lambda I)x=A*y+lambda D(x).
limitations: Eight CG iterations approximate each solve; three unrolls and synthetic Cartesian two-coil data.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

51.name: VarNet
51.mechanism: Original fastMRI sensitivity estimation and normalized-U-Net k-space cascades.
limitations: Two cascades, smaller widths and four calibration lines; synthetic phantom MSE replaces the original benchmark training loss/data.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

52.name: DnCNN
52.mechanism: Author-recommended DnCNN code predicts the additive noise residual and subtracts it from the observation.
limitations: Seventeen convolution layers retained, width reduced from 64 to 8; no pretrained weights.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

53.name: Noise2Noise
53.mechanism: Regress a second independent unclipped zero-mean noisy acquisition from the first; clean data is not read by the loss.
limitations: Compact U-Net instead of the original TensorFlow architecture; independence is a dataset assumption, not inferred from image appearance.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

54.name: Noise2Self
54.mechanism: Nine disjoint pixel subsets are masked; predictions on J do not depend on any measured input in J.
limitations: Deterministic zero replacement and a compact U-Net; full J-invariant inference needs nine forward passes.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

55.name: DDPM
55.mechanism: Original linear beta schedule, epsilon-MSE objective and consecutive ancestral reverse transitions.
limitations: Compact time-conditioned U-Net; default prior training uses 1000 time indices, and ancestral generation requires all 1000 steps.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

56.name: DDIM
56.mechanism: The same DDPM epsilon objective feeds a separate non-Markovian sampler; eta=0 is deterministic conditional on initial noise.
limitations: No distinct DDIM training objective; twenty-step generation is a speed/accuracy setting, not a reproduced benchmark.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

57.name: Score-SDE
57.mechanism: Continuous VP marginal noising and denoising score matching; reverse SDE and probability-flow ODE have different score coefficients.
limitations: VP branch and Euler integration only; original predictor-corrector networks and published settings are not recreated.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

59.name: DDRM
59.mechanism: Three spectral reverse-update cases condition a diffusion prior on noisy measurements and zero/nonzero singular values.
limitations: Exactly diagonal binary inpainting operator with unit nonzero singular values; a useful pretrained prior is not supplied.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

60.name: DPS
60.mechanism: Differentiate measurement discrepancy through the Tweedie x0 estimate, then guide consecutive DDPM sampling updates.
limitations: Binary inpainting and Gaussian noise example; training_loss trains the prior, reconstruct() runs posterior sampling separately.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

62.name: Flow Matching
62.mechanism: Conditional optimal-transport Gaussian path and analytical velocity regression require no training-time ODE solve.
limitations: Small positive sigma_min leaves endpoint smoothing; this is the conditional OT path, not every flow-matching variant.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

63.name: Rectified Flow
63.mechanism: Regress straight noise/data path velocities; reflow_pairs explicitly recouples a trained ODE's initial and terminal samples.
limitations: Default smoke training is first-round rectified flow; iterative reflow requires user-run endpoint generation and retraining.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

64.name: Consistency Models
64.mechanism: Shared-noise adjacent sigma pairs, a stop-gradient EMA target, and exact sigma_min boundary parameterization.
limitations: Fixed sixteen-level consistency-training grid and MSE; no pretrained diffusion distillation or original progressive schedule.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

65.name: DiT
65.mechanism: Original patch Transformer, time/class embeddings and adaLN-Zero backbone, trained with epsilon prediction.
limitations: Two Transformer blocks on small image pixels; no pretrained latent VAE. Original code is CC BY-NC 4.0, not MIT.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

66.name: Spatial Transformer Network
66.mechanism: Identity-initialized localization network predicts affine parameters for differentiable grid generation and resampling.
limitations: Synthetic 2D alignment rather than classification; affine grid coordinates are normalized, not patient millimetres.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

67.name: VoxelMorph
67.mechanism: A 3D encoder-decoder predicts a dense displacement; image similarity plus spatial smoothness trains through warping.
limitations: Reduced U-Net, known synthetic translations and normalized coordinates; no pretrained VoxelMorph or diffeomorphic integration.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

68.name: GradICON
68.mechanism: Bidirectional warps are composed and the spatial derivative of composition error is penalized.
limitations: Finite-difference Jacobians and a small shared network; no original multistep registration architecture or topology guarantee.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

70.name: DiffPose
70.mechanism: A pose initializer and test-time gradient refinement share a differentiable rigid volume projector.
limitations: Normalized parallel-beam renderer; no calibrated cone-beam DiffDRR, patient-specific published pretraining or geodesic pose loss.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

71.name: X2CT-GAN
71.mechanism: Two orthogonal image encoders lift features along their missing axes; 3D fusion uses adversarial, voxel and projection losses.
limitations: Small custom encoders/decoder, synthetic orthogonal mean projections; not the original chest-CT model, and two views are required.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

72.name: NeRF
72.mechanism: Coordinate/direction-conditioned density and radiance integrate using exclusive transmittance and emission-absorption compositing.
limitations: One synthetic scene; compact MLP and uniform finite-interval rays; no hierarchical coarse/fine sampling or original benchmark training.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

73.name: NAF
73.mechanism: A position-only hash-encoded attenuation field fits cone-ray line-integral measurements, with Beer-Lambert transmission exp(-integral).
limitations: Normalized synthetic attenuation values; no scanner calibration, CUDA marching or original CBCT architecture/configuration.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

74.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting
74.mechanism: Perspective Jacobians project anisotropic 3D Gaussian covariances; depth-sorted opacities alpha-compose colors.
limitations: Dense CPU rasterizer with sixteen Gaussians; no CUDA tile renderer, densification, pruning or nonconstant spherical harmonics.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

75.name: GCN
75.mechanism: Symmetrically degree-normalized neighbor aggregation with added self-loops.
limitations: Direct PyG GCNConv; independently sampled small graphs replace citation/medical datasets.

76.name: GAT
76.mechanism: Masked additive attention over each node neighborhood, with multiple attention heads.
limitations: Direct PyG GATConv; two heads/two layers on small graphs. No paper benchmark claim.

77.name: LSTM
77.mechanism: Input/forget/output gates and an additive memory cell carry information across time.
limitations: Direct modern PyTorch LSTM includes forget gates introduced after the 1997 paper; this historical difference is explicit. Synthetic waves are not ECG/EEG.

78.name: Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN)
78.mechanism: Author residual causal convolutions use exponentially increasing dilation and weight normalization.
limitations: Unmodified author TemporalConvNet with 3 small channel stages and a new task head. Synthetic waves; no paper benchmark.

79.name: HeartBEiT (downstream image architecture)
79.mechanism: The author's MIT-attributed BEiT classification encoder receives rasterized synthetic traces; relative position bias, layer scale and mean token pooling are retained.
limitations: Architecture-only exercise: HeartBEiT's DALL-E tokenization, ECG masked pretraining, pretrained weights and cardiac downstream studies are not reproduced.
The default uses four dimensionless synthetic waveform traces rendered on a 64x64 grid; these are not physiological ECGs or calibrated paper ECG images.
Width/depth/patch size are reduced; random weights carry no foundation-model capability.
Only modeling_finetune.py has been copied under its explicit file-level Microsoft MIT notice; the repository's remaining files have no inferred redistribution permission.

80.name: LaBraM (downstream EEG architecture)
80.mechanism: The authors' TemporalConv and NeuralTransformer operate on channel-by-time patches with separate learned electrode and time embeddings and Q/K normalization.
limitations: Architecture-only exercise: VQ neural tokenizer, masked code prediction, full pretraining corpus and pretrained LaBraM capability are not reproduced.
Synthetic waveforms are interpolated to two 200-sample patches per channel. This is a shape adapter, not an assertion of EEG sampling rate or a source of extra information.
Synthetic channel IDs 1..C have no anatomical electrode identity. Real EEG requires explicit montage, channel-order, unit and sampling checks.
Width 100 and depth two replace the original base preset; all weights are random.

81.name: VGG-16/19
81.mechanism: Upstream make_layers with the VGG-16 D configuration, reduced channels and three-layer classifier.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Default runs VGG-16; set variant=19 for VGG-19. Adaptive pooling 1x1 and narrow classifier replace the original head.

82.name: GoogLeNet / Inception-v1
82.mechanism: Upstream GoogLeNet multi-branch Inception modules and global pooling.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Auxiliary classifiers and dropout disabled; torchvision's documented implementation details differ from the original Caffe model.

83.name: ResNeXt
83.mechanism: Upstream ResNet Bottleneck class configured with grouped 3x3 transforms (cardinality 8).
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
One bottleneck per stage, cardinality 8 and base width 4; not the original 32x4d preset.

84.name: SENet
84.mechanism: timm SE-ResNet-18 with global squeeze and sigmoid channel excitation inside residual blocks.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
SE-ResNet-18 family example, not SENet-154; one-channel input and three classes.

85.name: EfficientNet
85.mechanism: Upstream MBConv, squeeze-excitation and compound width/depth configuration.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Quarter width/half depth B0-family teaching configuration is not a published EfficientNet checkpoint.

86.name: U-Net++
86.mechanism: Nested decoder grid concatenates all earlier same-scale nodes, with supervised heads at each decoder depth.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Three-level, narrow independent port; original pruning/clinical experiments and nnU-Net trainer not reproduced.

87.name: Attention U-Net
87.mechanism: MONAI additive spatial attention gates filter encoder skip tensors with decoder context.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Three resolution levels, width 8; MONAI implementation and synthetic foreground classes.

88.name: H-DenseUNet (hybrid fusion mechanism)
88.mechanism: 2D dense encoder/decoder features are stacked in slice order and fused with 3D dense features before a volumetric head.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Compact independent hybrid port; staged ImageNet/LiTS training, original DenseNet depths and liver/tumor experiment are not reproduced.

89.name: DeiT (distillation mechanism)
89.mechanism: timm distilled ViT has separate class/distillation tokens and heads; hard teacher targets supervise the distillation head.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
Default teacher is an explicit analytic classifier of synthetic shape fill ratio, not the paper's pretrained RegNetY. Supply teacher_logits for a real teacher.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

90.name: Pyramid Vision Transformer / PVT
90.mechanism: Authors' PVT v1 class: four pyramid stages, spatial-reduction attention and last-stage class token.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
CPU dimensions differ from the paper's training preset; see the explicit configuration.

91.name: SegFormer
91.mechanism: Authors' overlapping Mix Transformer encoder, depthwise Mix-FFN and all-MLP multi-scale decode head.
limitations: Random initialization and synthetic data; no original benchmark result or pretrained capability is reproduced.
NVIDIA vendor code permits noncommercial research/evaluation only; see vendor/image_segformer/LICENSE.
MMCV registry/checkpoint interfaces removed; SyncBatchNorm becomes ordinary BatchNorm on one CPU; dimensions reduced.

92.name: BEiT
92.mechanism: Masked patch prediction uses discrete target tokens instead of pixels.
limitations: Teaching tokenizer is fixed patch-intensity quantization, NOT the pretrained dVAE tokenizer. Demonstrates the discrete-target objective only; no claim of BEiT architecture or result equivalence.

93.name: BYOL
93.mechanism: Online encoder/projector/predictor regresses to an EMA target, with target stop-gradient and symmetric views.
limitations: Readable CPU mechanism port replaces author JAX training; tiny patch encoder, no BN or original augmentations/schedules.

94.name: SwAV
94.mechanism: Entropy-regularized balanced Sinkhorn assignments from one view supervise prototype scores in the other.
limitations: Small two-view experiment; no multi-crop queue/distributed training. Tiny batches are an objective exercise, not evidence of learned transfer.

95.name: ALIGN
95.mechanism: Pinned Transformers ALIGN: seven-stage EfficientNet MBConv/SE image tower, BERT text tower, normalized embeddings, learned temperature and symmetric label-smoothed contrastive loss.
limitations: Canonical Apache-2.0 library implementation follows the Kakao Brain reproduction; it is not Google's unreleased original training implementation or checkpoint.

Reduced width/depth with random initialization, 32-token synthetic vocabulary and two paired images replace web-scale noisy image-text training. All seven EfficientNet stage types remain; each has at least one block.

Vision initializer std=0.1 replaces the library's checkpoint-oriented 0.02, whose deep uncalibrated random tower can underflow during evaluation. Synthetic images use [-1,1] normalization without original data augmentation; no foundation retrieval or zero-shot performance is established.

113.name: Noise2Void
113.mechanism: Neighbourhood replacement removes selected central observations from the input; only those held-out targets contribute to loss.
limitations: Randomized regular partitions ensure no selected pixel leaks through another replacement; smaller U-Net and modified mask sampling.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

114.name: RED-Net
114.mechanism: Symmetric convolution/deconvolution stacks carry mirrored additive feature skips and a residual image path.
limitations: Ten layers, small channels and simplified every-second-depth skips; not the full RED30 architecture/training.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

115.name: SwinIR
115.mechanism: Original residual Swin Transformer blocks, alternating shifted windows, relative position bias and reconstruction head.
limitations: Two two-block stages, 24 embedding channels and 4px windows; denoising task only, no pretrained super-resolution model.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

116.name: Restormer
116.mechanism: Original multiscale Restormer with channel-transposed MDTA attention and gated depthwise-convolution feed-forward blocks.
limitations: Width 8 and one block per level; no pretrained restoration weights.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

117.name: AUTOMAP
117.mechanism: Dense sensor-to-image layers learn a global complex Fourier-to-image transform, followed by convolutional refinement.
limitations: A 16px complete synthetic Fourier acquisition; reduced layer/kernel sizes and no original manifold-pretraining/data augmentation.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

118.name: LEARN
118.mechanism: Each stage combines its own three-layer CNN regularizer with an explicit A-transpose projection residual.
limitations: Three unrolls and a pixel-driven parallel-beam operator; positive step parameters are bounded through softplus scaling.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

119.name: DDNM
119.mechanism: Replace estimated x0's measurement-range component with A-dagger y while retaining its null-space component.
limitations: Noiseless inpainting where A-dagger=A; DDNM+ noisy-data and time-travel variants are not included.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

120.name: RealNVP
120.mechanism: Alternating affine coupling layers give exact inverse transforms and exact triangular-Jacobian log determinants.
limitations: Vectorized single-scale coupling, uniform dequantization, small MLPs; no original multiscale image architecture.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

121.name: Glow
121.mechanism: Squeeze, data-initialized ActNorm, invertible learned 1x1 mixing and affine coupling provide exact likelihood and inversion.
limitations: One scale, full matrix determinant/inverse rather than LU acceleration, no hierarchical latent splits.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

122.name: PFGM++
122.mechanism: A Beta(N/2,D/2) radial perturbation law and EDM-preconditioned denoising learn the finite-D augmented Poisson field.
limitations: Finite augmented dimension D=64 and compact network; original PFGM corresponds to D=1, not a D-to-zero limit; no full ODE sampler.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

123.name: SiT
123.mechanism: Original SiT Transformer with velocity regression on its linear stochastic-interpolant path.
limitations: Two blocks on pixels; no pretrained VAE or alternative score/noise parameterizations and SDE samplers.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

124.name: LapIRN
124.mechanism: Three coarse-to-fine registration stages warp previous estimates and compose residual displacement corrections.
limitations: Small custom networks and displacement composition; not the original Laplacian residual-feature decoder or diffeomorphic variant.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

125.name: TransMorph
125.mechanism: Original four-level 3D Swin hierarchy, convolutional decoder, transformer/convolution skips and voxel-unit SpatialTransformer, trained with original MSE plus Grad3d loss.
limitations: 32-cubed resampled synthetic volumes; embedding width8, two blocks per level, 2-cubed windows and no stochastic depth; both directions accumulated into one optimizer step. Raw flow components are D/H/W voxel displacements; normalized_xyz_flow converts them explicitly.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

126.name: IDIR
126.mechanism: A SIREN coordinate network fits one image pair's displacement at test time with autograd spatial derivatives.
limitations: Only the first synthetic pair is fitted; smoothness regularization rather than every original Jacobian/bending variant; normalized coordinates.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

128.name: pixelNeRF
128.mechanism: Project world points into a known reference camera, sample aligned CNN features and condition a radiance field for a new view.
limitations: Single reference view, small encoder/MLP and synthetic scenes; no original ResNet encoder or multiview feature aggregation.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

129.name: Instant-NGP
129.mechanism: Learnable multiresolution hash tables interpolate features at eight cell corners before a small radiance decoder.
limitations: CPU PyTorch implementation; no fused CUDA kernels, occupancy skipping or claimed real-time performance.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

131.name: EndoNeRF
131.mechanism: A time-dependent deformation maps observations to a canonical radiance field; synthetic occlusions mask RGB/depth supervision.
limitations: One synthetic moving phantom; no clinical stereo preprocessing, tool segmentation or original depth-guided importance sampler.
Synthetic teaching data only; no clinical validity or published benchmark is claimed.

132.name: GraphSAGE
132.mechanism: A learned root transform and mean-neighbor aggregation support inductive node prediction.
limitations: Direct PyG SAGEConv; uses all neighbors on tiny graphs instead of stochastic large-graph sampling.

133.name: Graphormer
133.mechanism: Graph attention receives shortest-path spatial bias and degree/centrality embeddings.
limitations: Independent mechanism subset: no multi-hop edge-feature encoding, graph-token objective, original training or medical mesh decoder.

136.name: GRU
136.mechanism: Update and reset gates control recurrent state without a separate cell state.
limitations: Direct PyTorch GRU applies reset after the recurrent linear map; the Cho et al. original formulation places it before. Not claimed bitwise equivalent to that original equation.

137.name: ECGFounder (Net1D architecture)
137.mechanism: The authors' Net1D: SAME-padded grouped 1D bottlenecks, squeeze-excitation, residual downsampling, global time pooling and a task head.
limitations: Architecture-only exercise: no ten-million-recording pretraining, 150-label diagnostic ontology, lead-dropout pretraining or published checkpoint is included.
The default reads one synthetic waveform channel; it is not a physiological ECG or a validated single-lead disease predictor.
Original seven-stage block counts and kernel size 16 are retained, but channels are reduced and the downstream head has three synthetic classes.
No external weights are loaded. Low compute does not recreate the learned knowledge of ECGFounder.
